1 package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner; 2 3 import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Val; 4 import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner; 5 6 /** 7 * Runs after {@link BuildOwner} on {@code POST /api/owners} and stamps the new owner's 8 * {@code householdId}. 9 * 10 *

The id is deterministic: it is computed by {@link OwnerHousehold#householdId()} from the 11 * owner's {@code lastName} and {@code postcode} alone, so two owners with the same last name and 12 * postcode receive the same {@code householdId} automatically — there is no longer any lookup of an 13 * existing household to join or any minted/donated identifier, and {@code sharesHousehold} no longer 14 * affects the id (it only governs whether a second member of a household is treated as an 15 * acknowledged member rather than a suspected duplicate; see {@link CheckPossibleDuplicate}). An owner 16 * with no postcode has no household to key on and is left with a {@code null} {@code householdId}. 17 * 18 *

The {@code householdId} is a component of the owner's 19 * {@link org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.OwnerIdentity} key and is the single value that 20 * duplicate detection and the household-size count ({@link CountHouseholdMembers}) key off. 21 */ 22 public class AssignHousehold { 23 24 public void service(@Val Owner owner) { 25 owner.setHouseholdId(OwnerHousehold.of(owner).householdId()); 26 } 27 } 28

content.text:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The behaviour-level redesign is placed roughly where it belongs (Soundex extracted to its own model class, identity logic kept inside `OwnerIdentity`, soft-match kept inside `CheckPossibleDuplicate`), but the change introduces duplication and leaves sibling classes describing a world that no longer exists.

**1. `sha256hex` is now copy-pasted verbatim into `OwnerIdentity`.**
`OwnerIdentity.sha256hex` (model/OwnerIdentity.java:45-60) is byte-for-byte identical to `OwnerHousehold.sha256hex` (rest/function/owner/OwnerHousehold.java:58-73) — same body, same javadoc, same `NoSuchAlgorithmException` handling. Before this change `OwnerIdentity` built its key by string concatenation and had no hashing; the diff copied the helper rather than sharing it. Extract one shared helper (e.g. a small `Sha256`/hex util next to `OwnerIdentity` in the model package) and call it from both. As written, the two hex-encoding routines can silently drift.

**2. `OwnerHousehold`'s "single definition of same household" doc is now false.**
Its class javadoc (OwnerHousehold.java:22-25) still names `CheckPossibleDuplicate` among the steps that key off `householdId`, and claims changing the keying rule "happens here, once." But `CheckPossibleDuplicate` no longer touches `OwnerHousehold`/`householdId` at all — it matches on `soundex(lastName) + postcode` directly. A maintainer editing `OwnerHousehold` to change household matching would not realize the soft-match path is now unaffected. Update the doc to reflect that only `CountHouseholdMembers`/`CapMembershipLevel` still key off it.

**3. `AssignHousehold`'s doc still claims `householdId` feeds the identity key.**
AssignHousehold.java:18-20 states "The `householdId` is a component of the owner's `OwnerIdentity` key and is the single value that duplicate detection … key off." After this change `OwnerIdentity` no longer uses `householdId`, and duplicate detection (hard and soft) no longer keys off it. This is now actively misleading and should be corrected to scope `householdId` to the household-size count.

**4. Postcode normalization re-inlined, bypassing the shared household key.**
`CheckPossibleDuplicate.normalizePostcode` (`postcode.strip()`, lines 65-67) re-implements the exact postcode normalization `OwnerHousehold` centralizes (`postcode.strip()` in its compact constructor). The soft-match is conceptually a household-similarity key ("surname sound + postcode"), yet it's computed inline here instead of through the abstraction that exists precisely to hold that rule "once." Either express the soundex+postcode match through a shared helper (mirroring `OwnerHousehold`) or, at minimum, don't duplicate the postcode-normalization rule in a second place where it can diverge from `OwnerHousehold`.

Fixing #1 (shared hash helper) and reconciling the stale docs in #2/#3 are the most important; #4 is the judgment call about keeping household keying in one unit.
